title: Marketplace Quick Primer + Partner Onboarding Checklist
summary: Compact, execution-focused checklist and copy primer to onboard partners and validate cloud marketplace listings across AWS/GCP/Azure. Designed for quick preflight by partner managers + ops before handing to legal and engineering for final sign-off.
content: Purpose: This doc centralizes the minimum viable steps, copy options, and technical acceptance criteria needed to get a partner listing into a cloud marketplace (trial, paid SKU, or free tier). Use this as the canonical 'quick primer' for small launches and fast secondaries to avoid rework. Tone: pragmatic, task-oriented; call out owners and test steps explicitly so we can run through a 30–90 minute preflight with a partner. Scope: Hosted product listings (Redwood Hosted API + Dedicated offering variants). Not intended to replace full legal/compliance intake for enterprise Private deployments; those require the security intake flow.
checklist: Partner kickoff: confirm partner contact, legal POA, and target marketplace(s)
SKU mapping: define 1–3 SKUs (trial, monthly, committed) and internal SKU alias used for billing routing
Copy lock: finalize short description (<= 280 chars), long description (400–800 chars), and 2–3 bullets focused on value props
Logo + hero: obtain 1200x600 PNG and 512x512 square icon; confirm transparent background preference
Screenshot set: provide 3 annotated screenshots + 1 architecture diagram (800x600 min)
Integration guide: 1-page quickstart (curl + SDK snippet) and link to full docs
Security checklist: SOC/ISO statements, TLS cert notes, data residency options, and KMS/HSM support detail
Billing & metering: confirm price units (per-token, per-embed), meter granularity, and billing thresholds for trial conversion
Legal agreements: partner MSA or marketplace marketplace-specific contract template uploaded to legal ops
Testing plan: staging listing created and validated end-to-end (purchase flow, API keys, usage reporting)
Localization: decide 1–2 locales for launch (en-US required), flag planned i18n work
Compliance badges: verify required attestations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA if claimed) and supporting docs
Go/no-go review: schedule slotted 30-minute review with GTM, legal, product, and infra owners
copy_snippets: Short description (280c): Redwood Inference: fast, predictable LLM inference with predictable cost and enterprise controls—hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.

Long description (400–800c): Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for production-grade LLM serving. Ship features with consistent latency and cost controls across hosted API, reserved Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Built-in observability, automatic fallbacks, and model lifecycle tooling reduce operational risk and unit cost for teams in regulated or high-throughput environments.

Bullets (value props): 1) Latency SLOs & autoscaling for real workloads; 2) Cost controls via batching, caching, and quantization guidance; 3) Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; 4) Enterprise-grade security & audit logs
CTA examples: Start a free trial, Request Dedicated capacity, Schedule a technical onboarding
SEO-friendly tagline: High-performance LLM inference for production applications
technical_prereqs: API endpoint variants documented (hosted, dedicated, regional endpoints) and sample curl commands included
API key flow: activation, rate limits, quotas for trial accounts defined
Service health page URL and status page integration (where applicable)
Model catalog mapping: list of eligible model IDs for marketplace listing and fallback policy defined
Telemetry hooks: where billing events, request_id, and latency metrics will be emitted for marketplace metering
Deployment options: note whether Dedicated or Private SKUs require separate provisioning pipelines and expected lead times
CORS and CSP guidance for any embedded console UIs included in listing
legal_prereqs: Signed partner MSA or marketplace contract copy uploaded to legal ops
Data processing addendum (DPA) for EU customers if personal data is expected
Claims matrix: approved marketing claims + disallowed language (no absolutes like 'always'/'guaranteed')
Export controls: confirm that partner use cases and data flows comply with export rules
PII handling statement and retention policy brief included
ui_assets_required: Hero banner (1200x600 JPG/PNG) with safe text area
3 product screenshots with captions and short usage callouts
1 architecture/attachment diagram (SVG/PDF) showing data flow and optional VPC components
Support/contact card (email + docs link) formatted for marketplace entry
test_plan: Staging listing: create and verify listing metadata (descriptions, tags, categories) in marketplace staging portal
Purchase test: complete a purchase (trial or paid) and validate provisioning and API key issuance
Metering test: generate usage that maps to billing events and verify reporting latency <= 5 minutes
Failure modes: simulate quota exhaustion and verify user-facing messaging and fallback behavior
Region test: exercise endpoints in target regions and confirm latency meets stated guidance
Support flow: open a support ticket from marketplace console and confirm routing to Redwood support queue

open_questions: Do we support 14-day free trials with automatic conversion or manual opt-in? (impact: billing integration)
Which model variants are approved for marketplace usage in EU regions to satisfy data residency?
Should we publish an example pricing calculator tile in the listing or link to an external pricing page?
Is a dedicated SaaS screenshot walkthrough required for Azure marketplace bundling?
Do we need an explicit security architecture diagram for GCP marketplace policy review?
notes: Keep this doc lightweight — use as a preflight before full marketplace runbook is invoked
If partner requires Private deployment, trigger security intake immediately and expect 4–8 week provisioning lead time
For rapid launches, prioritize short description, one high-quality hero, and the curl quickstart; other assets can land in week 2 post-launch
